decisions.reason: The verb means to declare someone in the right. The people acknowledged that God's way, shown in John's call to repent, was right. The same verb returns in 7:35.

decisions.choice: who heard: who heard Jesus's words about John
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Jesus has just spoken about John to the crowds (7:24), and the people who had accepted John's baptism agreed.

decisions.choice: tax collectors: Jews who collected taxes for Rome or its rulers, and were despised
decisions.reason: As in 3:12 and 5:27-30, these were people others looked down on. They had come to John to be baptized (3:12).

decisions.choice: agreed that God was in the right (B); agreed that God's way was right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "justifying" God means, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: heard Jesus say this
decisions.reason: Readable says what they heard, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: publicanos (L); cobradores de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Literal keeps the traditional word, Balanced and Readable say what these men did (meaning decision m4). The same in verse 34.

decisions.choice: declararon justo a Dios
decisions.reason: "Declared God right" (meaning decision m2). "Justificar" in Spanish now usually means to excuse, which would point the wrong way.

decisions.choice: justifièrent Dieu (L); reconnut que Dieu était dans son droit (B); ont reconnu que le chemin de Dieu était le bon (R)
alternatives: déclarèrent Dieu juste (B), as the style guide's term for justification
decisions.reason: Here it is God who is "justified": people declare that he is right (m2). The style guide's "déclarer juste" is for God declaring people righteous; used of God it would sound as if they judged him. Literal keeps the verb; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: les collecteurs d’impôts (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the New Testament: "publicains" is a church word that most readers no longer understand.

decisions.choice: walimkiri Mungu kuwa mwenye haki (L); walikubali kwamba Mungu yuko sahihi (B, R)
decisions.reason: They declared that God was right (meaning decision m2). "Kuhesabiwa haki" is the phrase for being made righteous before God, which would point the wrong way when said of God; Literal says they acknowledged him to be just.

decisions.choice: watoza ushuru
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the tax collectors (meaning decision m4), the same at every level. The same in verse 34.

decisions.choice: "xưng Đức Chúa Trời là công chính" (L); "nhìn nhận Đức Chúa Trời là đúng" (B); "đồng ý rằng đường lối của Đức Chúa Trời là đúng" (R)
alternatives: "xưng công bình cho Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Paul uses for "justify", but here people declare that God is right (meaning decision); Literal keeps the word for righteousness, "công chính", and Balanced and Readable say what is meant.

decisions.choice: 7:29-30 kept outside the quotation, which closed at the end of 7:28
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads these verses as the narrator's comment, so the Vietnamese, like the English, closes the quotation before them and opens it again in 7:31.

decisions.choice: "하나님께서 옳으시다고 인정하였다" (L, B); "하나님의 뜻이 옳다고 인정하였다" (R) for "justified God"
decisions.reason: To justify God is to declare that God is in the right (meaning decision); "의롭다 하다" is the word for God justifying people and would mislead here. The narrator's comment stands outside Jesus's speech, so the quotation closed at 7:28.

decisions.choice: "세리들" (L, B); "세금 걷는 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Luke 5:27-30 in Korean.

decisions.choice: reconheceram que Deus estava certo
decisions.reason: The style table gives "declarar justo" for this verb at Balanced, but with God as the object it would sound as if people passed a verdict on him. As m2 explains, they acknowledged that God's way was right; Balanced says so, as the English does. Literal keeps "justificaram a Deus".

decisions.choice: "እግዚአብሔርን አጸደቁ" (they justified God) at Literal
decisions.reason: "አጸደቀ" is the verb of the same family as "ጽድቅ" (righteousness) and means to declare someone in the right, which is the Greek verb here; Balanced and Readable say it plainly, as the English does.

source.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς, μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The but Pharisees and the lawyers the purpose of the God rejected for themselves, not having been baptized by him.

en.L: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law set aside the purpose of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
en.B: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law refused what God intended for them, since they had not let John baptize them.
en.R: But the Pharisees and the experts in God's law turned away from what God wanted to do for them. They would not let John baptize them.

es.L: Pero los fariseos y los expertos en la ley rechazaron para sí mismos el propósito de Dios, no habiendo sido bautizados por él.
es.B: Pero los fariseos y los expertos en la ley rechazaron lo que Dios quería para ellos, pues no se habían dejado bautizar por Juan.
es.R: Pero los fariseos y los expertos en la ley de Dios se apartaron de lo que Dios quería hacer por ellos. No quisieron que Juan los bautizara.

fr.L: Mais les Pharisiens et les experts de la Loi rejetèrent pour eux-mêmes le dessein de Dieu, n’ayant pas été baptisés par lui.
fr.B: Mais les Pharisiens et les experts de la Loi refusèrent ce que Dieu voulait pour eux, puisqu’ils ne s’étaient pas fait baptiser par Jean.
fr.R: Mais les Pharisiens et les experts de la Loi ont refusé ce que Dieu voulait faire pour eux. Ils n’ont pas voulu que Jean les baptise.

sw.L: Lakini Mafarisayo na wataalamu wa sheria walilikataa kusudi la Mungu kwa ajili yao wenyewe, kwa kuwa hawakubatizwa naye.
sw.B: Lakini Mafarisayo na wataalamu wa sheria walikataa kile ambacho Mungu alikusudia kwa ajili yao, kwa kuwa hawakukubali kubatizwa na Yohana.
sw.R: Lakini Mafarisayo na wataalamu wa sheria ya Mungu walikiacha kile ambacho Mungu alitaka kuwafanyia. Hawakukubali Yohana awabatize.

vi.L: nhưng những người Pha-ri-si và các chuyên gia luật pháp đã gạt bỏ ý định của Đức Chúa Trời cho chính họ, vì đã không chịu ông làm báp-têm.
vi.B: Nhưng những người Pha-ri-si và các chuyên gia luật pháp đã khước từ điều Đức Chúa Trời muốn làm cho họ, vì họ không chịu để Giăng làm báp-têm cho mình.
vi.R: Nhưng những người Pha-ri-si và các chuyên gia về luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời đã quay lưng với điều Đức Chúa Trời muốn làm cho họ. Họ không chịu để Giăng làm báp-têm cho mình.

ko.L: 그러나 바리새파 사람들과 율법 전문가들은 그에게 세례를 받지 않아서, 자기들을 위한 하나님의 뜻을 저버렸다.
ko.B: 그러나 바리새파 사람들과 율법 전문가들은 요한에게 세례를 받지 않았으므로, 하나님께서 자기들을 위해 세우신 뜻을 거절하였다.
ko.R: 그러나 바리새파 사람들과 하나님의 율법을 잘 아는 사람들은 요한에게 세례를 받으려고 하지 않았다. 그래서 하나님께서 그들을 위해 하시려는 일을 거부하였다.

pt.L: Mas os fariseus e os especialistas na Lei rejeitaram o propósito de Deus para si mesmos, não tendo sido batizados por ele.
pt.B: Mas os fariseus e os estudiosos da Lei recusaram o que Deus queria para eles, pois não tinham deixado que João os batizasse.
pt.R: Mas os fariseus e os especialistas na Lei de Deus rejeitaram o que Deus queria fazer por eles. Eles não deixaram João batizá-los.

am.L: ፈሪሳውያንና የሕግ አዋቂዎች ግን በእርሱ ስላልተጠመቁ የእግዚአብሔርን ሐሳብ ለራሳቸው ናቁ።
am.B: ፈሪሳውያንና የሕግ አዋቂዎች ግን ዮሐንስ እንዲያጠምቃቸው ስላልፈቀዱ እግዚአብሔር ለእነርሱ ያሰበውን አልተቀበሉም።
am.R: ፈሪሳውያንና የእግዚአብሔርን ሕግ የሚያውቁት ሰዎች ግን እግዚአብሔር ሊያደርግላቸው የፈለገውን ነገር ገፉ። ዮሐንስ እንዲያጠምቃቸው አልፈቀዱም።

decisions.choice: experts in the law: men trained in the law of Moses, much like the scribes
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for the experts who taught and applied God's law (10:25; 11:45-52). Many were Pharisees.

decisions.choice: the purpose of God: God's plan, here his call to repent through John
decisions.reason: The noun means a plan or decision. Luke uses it of God's saving plan (Acts 2:23; 20:27).

decisions.choice: for themselves: the plan was meant for them, and they rejected it
decisions.reason: The phrase can go with "rejected" (they rejected it, to their own loss) or with "purpose" (God's purpose for them). Either way they turned down what God offered them.

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement of Jews devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 6:2.

decisions.choice: experts in God's law (R); experts in the law (L, B)
decisions.reason: Today "lawyer" suggests courts and contracts. The word means someone expert in the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John, so the reader does not think of Jesus.

decisions.choice: los expertos en la ley
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for these men trained in the law of Moses (meaning decision m1), kept apart from "escribas" for the other word; Readable adds "de Dios" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: les experts de la Loi (every level)
decisions.reason: The word means men trained in the law of Moses (m1). "Juristes" suggests courts and contracts, "légistes" is rare, and "docteurs" now suggests medicine. The capital on "Loi" marks the Law of Moses; Readable keeps the same phrase, so that it stays apart from the Readable term for the scribes, "les spécialistes de la Loi".

decisions.choice: par Jean (B, R); par lui (L)
decisions.reason: As the English: French "lui" could be read as Jesus, so Balanced and Readable name John.

decisions.choice: wataalamu wa sheria
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for these men trained in the law of Moses (meaning decision m1), kept apart from "walimu wa sheria", the Readable word for the scribes; Readable adds "ya Mungu" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "các chuyên gia luật pháp" (L, B); "các chuyên gia về luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời" (R) for the lawyers
decisions.reason: Luke's word here is "those of the law", different from the scribes ("thầy thông giáo") and from the teachers of the law of 5:17 ("thầy dạy luật pháp"). "luật sư" now means an attorney; "chuyên gia" (expert) says what they were (meaning decision), as the English "experts in the law" does.

decisions.choice: "율법 전문가들" (L, B); "하나님의 율법을 잘 아는 사람들" (R) for nomikoi
decisions.reason: Luke uses a third word here, beside the scribes ("율법학자") and the teachers of the law ("율법 교사", 5:17); Korean keeps the three apart. The meaning decision says they were much like the scribes.

decisions.choice: os especialistas na Lei (L); os estudiosos da Lei (B); os especialistas na Lei de Deus (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, Luke's word for experts in the Law of Moses (also 10:25; 11:45-52; 14:3), worded as for the same word in Matthew 22:35.

decisions.choice: "የሕግ አዋቂዎች" (experts in the law)
alternatives: "የሕግ መምህራን" (teachers of the law, kept for the scribes)
decisions.reason: "ጠበቃ" is a modern courtroom lawyer, which these men were not. "የሕግ መምህራን" renders the scribes at Balanced and Readable, so a different phrase keeps the two Greek words apart, as in Matthew 22:35.

source.text: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι;

records.literal_gloss: To what then will I liken the people of the generation this, and to what are they like?

en.L: "To what then shall I compare the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation, and what are they like?
en.B: Jesus went on, "Then how shall I picture the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation? What are they like?
en.R: Jesus continued, "How can I describe the {{gender:people|men}} who live today? What are they like?

es.L: «¿Con qué, pues, compararé a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de esta generación, y a qué se parecen?
es.B: Jesús continuó: «¿Con qué compararé entonces a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de esta generación? ¿A qué se parecen?
es.R: Jesús siguió diciendo: «¿Cómo puedo describir a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que viven hoy? ¿A qué se parecen?

fr.L: « À quoi donc comparerai-je les {{gender:gens|hommes}} de cette génération, et à quoi ressemblent-ils ?
fr.B: Jésus poursuivit : « À quoi donc vais-je comparer les {{gender:gens|hommes}} de cette génération ? À quoi ressemblent-ils ?
fr.R: Jésus a continué : « À quoi est-ce que je peux comparer les {{gender:gens|hommes}} d’aujourd’hui ? À quoi ressemblent-ils ?

sw.L: "Basi niwafananishe watu wa kizazi hiki na nini, nao wanafanana na nini?
sw.B: Yesu aliendelea kusema, "Basi niwafananishe watu wa kizazi hiki na nini? Wao ni kama nini?
sw.R: Yesu aliendelea kusema, "Niwaelezeje watu wanaoishi siku hizi? Wao ni kama nini?

vi.L: "Vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ví người của thế hệ này với gì, và họ giống như gì?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói tiếp: "Vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ví người của thế hệ này với gì? Họ giống như gì?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói tiếp: "Ta có thể ví người ngày nay với gì? Họ giống như ai?

ko.L: "그러니 내가 이 세대 사람들을 무엇에 비기겠느냐? 그들은 무엇과 같으냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 계속 말씀하셨다. "그러면 이 세대 사람들을 무엇에 비길 수 있겠느냐? 그들은 무엇과 같으냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 계속 말씀하셨다. "지금 이 시대 사람들을 무엇에 비길 수 있겠느냐? 그들은 무엇과 같으냐?

pt.L: "A que, então, compararei {{gender:as pessoas|os homens}} desta geração, e com que se parecem?
pt.B: Jesus continuou: "Então, com que vou comparar {{gender:as pessoas|os homens}} desta geração? Com que se parecem?
pt.R: Jesus continuou: "Como posso descrever {{gender:as pessoas|os homens}} que vivem hoje? Com quem se parecem?

am.L: «እንግዲህ የዚህን ትውልድ ሰዎች በምን እመስላቸዋለሁ? ምንስ ይመስላሉ?
am.B: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ሲል ቀጠለ፦ «እንግዲህ የዚህን ትውልድ ሰዎች በምን ልመስላቸው? ምንንስ ይመስላሉ?
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ሲል ቀጠለ፦ «በዛሬ ጊዜ ያሉትን ሰዎች እንዴት ልግለጻቸው? ምንን ይመስላሉ?

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of Jesus's time, as a whole
alternatives: a period of thirty or forty years
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the people of his day who refused both John and himself (11:29-32; 17:25).

decisions.choice: two questions with one meaning
decisions.reason: The second question repeats the first, a Hebrew way of giving a saying weight.

decisions.choice: people: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus went on (B); Jesus continued (R)
decisions.reason: After the narrator's comment in 7:29-30, Balanced and Readable say that Jesus is speaking again. Literal only opens the quotation again.

decisions.choice: who live today
decisions.reason: Readable says what "generation" means here.

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has two wordings here, as English does: "las personas" for men and women (meaning decision m3), "los hombres" as the traditional form. "Las personas" rather than "la gente" keeps the plural verbs ("se parecen", "viven") the same under both settings.

decisions.choice: les {{gender:gens|hommes}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, men and women (m3). "Les humains de cette génération" would sound like a statement about the species; "les gens" is the ordinary inclusive word, with the traditional "les hommes" as the alternative. The article stays outside the span, since both read naturally.

decisions.choice: watu, no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has "people|men". "Watu" already means men and women (meaning decision m3), and "wanaume" would mean males only, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "người của thế hệ này" (L, B); "người ngày nay" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says human beings, men and women; "người" already says that, so the English gender span has no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: "예수께서 계속 말씀하셨다" (B, R)
alternatives: opening the quotation with no speaker
decisions.reason: After the narrator's comment of 7:29-30, Balanced and Readable say who is speaking again, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ሰዎች" (people) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Amharic "ሰዎች" already means men and women, which is what the Greek means here; "ወንዶች" (males) would say something the Greek does not, so there is no second wording for the setting to offer.

source.text: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις, ἃ λέγει· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε·

records.literal_gloss: Like they are to children who in marketplace are sitting and calling to one another, which says, We played the flute for you and not you danced; we sang a lament and not you wept.

en.L: They are like children sitting in [the] marketplace and calling to one another, who say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not weep.'
en.B: They are like small children who sit in the town square and shout to each other, 'We played wedding music on the flute for you, and you would not dance. We sang a funeral song, and you would not cry.'
en.R: They are like children sitting in the town square. They call out to each other, 'We played happy music on the flute for you, but you would not dance! We sang sad songs, but you would not cry!'

es.L: Se parecen a niños sentados en [la] plaza y que se gritan unos a otros, diciendo: “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos la flauta, y no {{plural_you:bailaron|bailasteis}}; entonamos lamentos, y no {{plural_you:lloraron|llorasteis}}”.
es.B: Son como niños pequeños que se sientan en la plaza del pueblo y se gritan unos a otros: “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos música de boda con la flauta, y no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} bailar. Cantamos un canto fúnebre, y no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} llorar”.
es.R: Son como niños sentados en la plaza del pueblo. Se gritan unos a otros: “¡{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos música alegre con la flauta, pero no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} bailar! ¡Cantamos canciones tristes, pero no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} llorar!”.

fr.L: Ils ressemblent à des enfants assis sur la place du marché et qui s’interpellent les uns les autres, qui disent : “Nous avons joué de la flûte pour vous, et vous n’avez pas dansé ; nous avons chanté un chant de deuil, et vous n’avez pas pleuré.”
fr.B: Ils sont comme de petits enfants assis sur la place, qui se lancent des appels les uns aux autres : “Nous avons joué pour vous un air de noce à la flûte, et vous n’avez pas voulu danser. Nous avons chanté un chant funèbre, et vous n’avez pas voulu pleurer.”
fr.R: Ils sont comme des enfants assis sur la place de la ville. Ils crient les uns aux autres : “Nous avons joué de la flûte pour vous, un air joyeux, mais vous n’avez pas voulu danser ! Nous avons chanté des chants tristes, mais vous n’avez pas voulu pleurer !”

sw.L: Wanafanana na watoto walioketi sokoni na kuitana wao kwa wao, wakisema, 'Tuliwapigia filimbi, nanyi hamkucheza; tuliomboleza, nanyi hamkulia.'
sw.B: Wao ni kama watoto wadogo wanaoketi uwanjani mjini na kuitana wao kwa wao, 'Tuliwapigia filimbi muziki wa harusi, lakini hamkutaka kucheza. Tuliimba wimbo wa maziko, lakini hamkutaka kulia.'
sw.R: Wao ni kama watoto walioketi uwanjani mjini. Wanaitana wao kwa wao, 'Tuliwapigia filimbi muziki wa furaha, lakini hamkutaka kucheza! Tuliimba nyimbo za huzuni, lakini hamkutaka kulia!'

vi.L: Họ giống như trẻ con ngồi ở chợ và gọi nhau, nói rằng: 'Chúng tôi đã thổi sáo cho các bạn mà các bạn không nhảy múa; chúng tôi đã hát bài ai ca mà các bạn không khóc.'
vi.B: Họ giống như những đứa trẻ ngồi ngoài chợ, gọi nhau mà nói: 'Bọn tớ thổi sáo nhạc đám cưới cho các bạn, mà các bạn chẳng chịu nhảy múa. Bọn tớ hát bài đám tang, mà các bạn chẳng chịu khóc.'
vi.R: Họ giống như mấy đứa trẻ ngồi ngoài chợ. Chúng gọi nhau và nói: 'Bọn tớ thổi sáo những bài vui cho các bạn, mà các bạn không chịu nhảy múa! Bọn tớ hát những bài buồn, mà các bạn không chịu khóc!'

ko.L: 그들은 장터에 앉아서 서로 부르며 이렇게 말하는 아이들과 같다. '우리가 너희에게 피리를 불어 주었는데도 너희는 춤추지 않았고, 우리가 곡을 하였는데도 너희는 울지 않았다.'
ko.B: 그들은 장터에 앉아서 서로 소리치는 어린아이들과 같다. '우리가 너희에게 잔치 피리를 불어 주었는데, 너희는 춤추지 않았다. 우리가 장례 노래를 불렀는데, 너희는 울지 않았다.'
ko.R: 그들은 마을 광장에 앉아 있는 아이들과 같다. 아이들은 서로 이렇게 소리친다. '우리가 너희에게 신나는 피리를 불어 주었는데, 너희는 춤을 추지 않았어! 우리가 슬픈 노래를 불렀는데, 너희는 울지 않았어!'

pt.L: São semelhantes a crianças sentadas na praça, que gritam umas para as outras, dizendo: 'Tocamos flauta para vocês, e vocês não dançaram; cantamos um lamento, e vocês não choraram.'
pt.B: São como crianças pequenas que se sentam na praça da cidade e gritam umas para as outras: 'Tocamos música de casamento na flauta para vocês, e vocês não quiseram dançar. Cantamos um canto fúnebre, e vocês não quiseram chorar.'
pt.R: São como crianças sentadas na praça. Elas gritam umas para as outras: 'Tocamos música alegre na flauta para vocês, mas vocês não quiseram dançar! Cantamos músicas tristes, mas vocês não quiseram chorar!'

am.L: በገበያ ስፍራ ተቀምጠው እርስ በርሳቸው የሚጠራሩ ልጆችን ይመስላሉ፤ እንዲህም ይላሉ፦ “ዋሽንት ነፋንላችሁ፤ አልጨፈራችሁምም፤ የሐዘን ዜማ አዜምን፤ አላለቀሳችሁምም።”
am.B: በከተማው አደባባይ ተቀምጠው እርስ በርሳቸው የሚጣሩ ትናንሽ ልጆችን ይመስላሉ፤ “የሠርግ ዜማ በዋሽንት ነፋንላችሁ፤ እናንተ ግን አልጨፈራችሁም። የለቅሶ ዜማ አዜምን፤ እናንተ ግን አላለቀሳችሁም።”
am.R: በከተማው አደባባይ የተቀመጡ ልጆችን ይመስላሉ። እርስ በርሳቸው እንዲህ ብለው ይጣራሉ፦ “የደስታ ሙዚቃ በዋሽንት ተጫወትንላችሁ፤ እናንተ ግን አልጨፈራችሁም! የሐዘን ዘፈን ዘፈንን፤ እናንተ ግን አላለቀሳችሁም!”

decisions.choice: the marketplace: the open square of a town, where people met and children played
decisions.reason: Every town had an open space for buying, selling and meeting.

decisions.choice: played the flute, sang a lament: children playing at weddings and at funerals
decisions.reason: Flute music went with weddings and feasts; wailing songs went with funerals. The children want the others to play their game, but the others will join in neither. So the people of this generation would accept neither John nor Jesus.

decisions.choice: which says: what the children call out
decisions.reason: The singular "says" goes with the neuter plural "children", as Greek allows.

decisions.choice: wedding music (B), happy music (R); a funeral song (B), sad songs (R)
alternatives: played the flute; sang a lament
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of game the children were playing, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans in the children's words
decisions.reason: The children call to the other children, a plural "you", so their words take the setting like Jesus's own.

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" (L); "bọn tớ" (B, R) and "các bạn" in the children's words
decisions.reason: Children at play speak to each other as "bọn tớ" and "các bạn"; Literal keeps the neutral "chúng tôi".

decisions.choice: "chợ" for the marketplace
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the open square where people met and children played; in a Vietnamese town that is the market, as in Mark 12:38.

decisions.choice: "피리를 불다", "곡을 하다" (L); "잔치 피리", "장례 노래" (B); "신나는 피리", "슬픈 노래" (R); the children speak in 해체 (R)
decisions.reason: Children played at weddings and at funerals (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Korean word for ritual wailing, "곡", and the other levels name the two games, as the English does. Readable lets the children speak as children do.

source.text: ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς μὴ ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον, καὶ λέγετε· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·

records.literal_gloss: Has come for John the Baptist not eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, A demon he has;

en.L: For John the Baptist has come not eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'
en.B: For John the Baptist has come eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, 'There is a demon in him.'
en.R: John the Baptist came, and he went without bread and did not drink wine. And you said, 'He has a demon in him!'

es.L: Porque ha venido Juan el Bautista sin comer pan ni beber vino, y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “Tiene un demonio”.
es.B: Porque ha venido Juan el Bautista, que no come pan ni bebe vino, y {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: “Tiene un demonio dentro”.
es.R: Juan el Bautista vino, y no comía pan ni bebía vino. Y {{plural_you:ustedes dijeron|vosotros dijisteis}}: “¡Tiene un demonio dentro!”.

fr.L: Car Jean le Baptiste est venu, ne mangeant pas de pain et ne buvant pas de vin, et vous dites : “Il a un démon.”
fr.B: En effet, Jean le Baptiste est venu ; il ne mangeait pas de pain et ne buvait pas de vin, et vous dites : “Il y a un démon en lui.”
fr.R: Jean le Baptiste est venu. Il se privait de pain et ne buvait pas de vin. Et vous avez dit : “Il a un démon en lui !”

sw.L: Kwa maana Yohana Mbatizaji amekuja bila kula mkate wala kunywa divai, nanyi mnasema, 'Ana pepo.'
sw.B: Kwa maana Yohana Mbatizaji amekuja, hali mkate wala hanywi divai, nanyi mnasema, 'Ana pepo ndani yake.'
sw.R: Yohana Mbatizaji alikuja, naye hakula mkate wala hakunywa divai. Nanyi mkasema, 'Ana pepo ndani yake!'

vi.L: Vì Giăng Báp-tít đã đến, không ăn bánh cũng không uống rượu, thì các người nói: 'Ông ta bị quỷ ám.'
vi.B: Vì Giăng Báp-tít đến, không ăn bánh, không uống rượu, thì các người nói: 'Ông ta bị quỷ ám.'
vi.R: Giăng Báp-tít đến, ông kiêng ăn bánh và không uống rượu. Thế mà các người nói: 'Ông ta bị quỷ ám!'

ko.L: 세례자 요한이 와서 빵도 먹지 않고 포도주도 마시지 않으니, 너희가 '그는 귀신이 들렸다' 하고 말한다.
ko.B: 세례자 요한이 와서 빵도 먹지 않고 포도주도 마시지 않자, 너희는 '그 사람은 귀신이 들렸다' 하고 말한다.
ko.R: 세례자 요한이 왔을 때, 그는 빵도 먹지 않고 포도주도 마시지 않았다. 그러자 너희는 '그 사람은 귀신이 들렸다!' 하고 말했다.

pt.L: Pois veio João Batista, não comendo pão nem bebendo vinho, e vocês dizem: 'Ele tem demônio.'
pt.B: Pois João Batista veio sem comer pão e sem beber vinho, e vocês dizem: 'Há um demônio nele.'
pt.R: João Batista veio, e ele ficava sem comer pão e não bebia vinho. E vocês disseram: 'Ele tem um demônio dentro dele!'

am.L: መጥምቁ ዮሐንስ እንጀራ ሳይበላ የወይን ጠጅም ሳይጠጣ መጥቷልና፤ እናንተም “ጋኔን አለበት” ትላላችሁ።
am.B: መጥምቁ ዮሐንስ እንጀራ ሳይበላና የወይን ጠጅ ሳይጠጣ መጥቷል፤ እናንተም “ጋኔን አድሮበታል” ትላላችሁ።
am.R: መጥምቁ ዮሐንስ መጣ፤ እንጀራ አልበላም፤ የወይን ጠጅም አልጠጣም። እናንተም “ጋኔን አለበት!” አላችሁ።

decisions.choice: not eating bread nor drinking wine: John lived a strict life of fasting
decisions.reason: John was to drink no wine (1:15), and he lived in the wilderness on simple food (Matthew 3:4). His disciples fasted often (5:33).

decisions.choice: he has a demon: he is mad, driven by an evil spirit
decisions.reason: People said the same of Jesus (John 7:20; 10:20). It dismissed John as out of his mind.

decisions.choice: past tense: came, said
decisions.reason: Readable tells it as a story of what happened.

decisions.choice: "bị quỷ ám" for "he has a demon"
decisions.reason: As in John 7:20 and 10:20: the usual Vietnamese phrase, which also carries the sense of madness the meaning decision gives.

decisions.choice: "귀신이 들렸다" for "he has a demon"
decisions.reason: Korean says of a possessed person that a demon "has entered" him, as in John 7:20 and 10:20 in Korean.

decisions.choice: "እንጀራ" (bread as food)
decisions.reason: The word list gives "እንጀራ" where bread stands for food in general and "ዳቦ" for loaves; here John's fasting from ordinary food is meant, so "እንጀራ" is used.

source.text: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγετε· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Has come the Son of the Man eating and drinking, and you say, Look, a man a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.

en.L: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look, a man who is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
en.B: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look at the man! He is greedy for food and a heavy drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
en.R: The Son of Man came, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ate and drank. And you said, 'Look at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! He eats too much and drinks too much wine. He is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

es.L: Ha venido el Hijo del Hombre comiendo y bebiendo, y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “Ahí está un hombre comilón y borracho, amigo de publicanos y pecadores”.
es.B: Ha venido el Hijo del Hombre, que come y bebe, y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} a ese hombre! Es un glotón y un gran bebedor, amigo de cobradores de impuestos y de pecadores”.
es.R: El Hijo del Hombre vino, y comía y bebía. Y {{plural_you:ustedes dijeron|vosotros dijisteis}}: “¡{{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}! Come demasiado y bebe demasiado vino. ¡Es amigo de cobradores de impuestos y de pecadores!”.

fr.L: Le Fils de l’homme est venu, mangeant et buvant, et vous dites : “Voici un homme glouton et ivrogne, ami des collecteurs d’impôts et des pécheurs.”
fr.B: Le Fils de l’homme est venu ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mange et boit, et vous dites : “Voyez cet homme ! C’est un gros mangeur et un grand buveur de vin, un ami des collecteurs d’impôts et des pécheurs !”
fr.R: Le Fils de l’homme est venu, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a mangé et bu. Et vous avez dit : “Regardez-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! Il mange trop et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} boit trop de vin. C’est un ami des collecteurs d’impôts et des pécheurs !”

sw.L: Mwana wa Adamu amekuja akila na kunywa, nanyi mnasema, 'Tazama, mtu mlafi na mlevi, rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi.'
sw.B: Mwana wa Adamu amekuja akila na kunywa, nanyi mnasema, 'Mwangalieni mtu huyu! Ni mlafi na mlevi, rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi!'
sw.R: Mwana wa Adamu alikuja, naye alikula na kunywa. Nanyi mkasema, 'Mwangalieni! Anakula kupita kiasi na kunywa divai kupita kiasi. Ni rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi!'

vi.L: Con Người đã đến, ăn và uống, thì các người nói: 'Kìa, một kẻ ham ăn và nghiện rượu, bạn của những người thu thuế và kẻ tội lỗi!'
vi.B: Con Người đến, ăn và uống, thì các người nói: 'Xem kìa! Người này ham ăn mê uống, là bạn của bọn thu thuế và kẻ tội lỗi!'
vi.R: Con Người đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn và uống. Thế mà các người nói: 'Xem ông ta kìa! Ông ta ăn quá nhiều và uống rượu quá nhiều. Ông ta là bạn của bọn thu thuế và những kẻ tội lỗi!'

ko.L: 인자는 와서 먹고 마시니, 너희가 말한다. '보라, 먹기를 탐하고 포도주를 즐기는 사람이다. 세리들과 죄인들의 친구다.'
ko.B: 인자는 와서 먹고 마시니, 너희는 '저 사람을 보아라! 먹을 것을 밝히고 술을 즐기는 사람이다. 세리들과 죄인들의 친구다!' 하고 말한다.
ko.R: 인자는 와서 먹기도 하고 마시기도 했다. 그러자 너희는 '저 사람을 보아라! 너무 많이 먹고 포도주도 너무 많이 마신다. 세금 걷는 사람들과 죄인들의 친구다!' 하고 말했다.

pt.L: Veio o Filho do Homem comendo e bebendo, e vocês dizem: 'Eis um homem comilão e beberrão, amigo de cobradores de impostos e de pecadores!'
pt.B: O Filho do Homem veio comendo e bebendo, e vocês dizem: 'Vejam só esse homem! Come demais e bebe demais, e é amigo de cobradores de impostos e de pecadores!'
pt.R: O Filho do Homem veio, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} comia e bebia. E vocês disseram: 'Olhem só para {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}! Come demais e bebe vinho demais. É amigo dos cobradores de impostos e dos pecadores!'

am.L: የሰው ልጅ እየበላና እየጠጣ መጥቷል፤ እናንተም “እነሆ፣ ሆዳምና ሰካራም ሰው፣ የቀራጮችና የኃጢአተኞች ጓደኛ!” ትላላችሁ።
am.B: የሰው ልጅ እየበላና እየጠጣ መጥቷል፤ እናንተም “እዩት! ሆዳምና ሰካራም ነው፤ የቀራጮችና የኃጢአተኞችም ጓደኛ ነው!” ትላላችሁ።
am.R: የሰው ልጅ መጣ፤ በላ፤ ጠጣም። እናንተም “እዩት! ከመጠን በላይ ይበላል፤ ብዙ የወይን ጠጅም ይጠጣል። የቀራጮችና የኃጢአተኞች ጓደኛ ነው!” አላችሁ።

decisions.choice: a glutton and a drunkard: the charge against a rebellious son in Deuteronomy 21:20
alternatives: a mere insult with no echo
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a stubborn son who is a glutton and a drunkard. The words brand Jesus as a disgrace to his people.

decisions.choice: a friend of tax collectors and sinners: one who shares meals with outcasts
alternatives: one who approves of their sins
decisions.reason: Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners (5:29-32), and he will do so again (7:36-50; 15:1-2; 19:7).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself, as in 5:24 and 6:5
decisions.reason: Jesus contrasts John's fasting with his own way of life, which was open to everyone.

decisions.choice: greedy for food and a heavy drinker (B); eats too much and drinks too much wine (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the old ones.

decisions.choice: Look (L); Look at the man (B); Look at him (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word points at Jesus with scorn, so Balanced and Readable keep it and say what is pointed at. "Behold" is old-fashioned.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m3), a title, never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Ahí está
decisions.reason: The people say "look" to one another, not to one person; "ahí está" points at him without choosing a singular or plural "you". Balanced and Readable say it to the group, with the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: le Fils de l’homme, with no gender setting (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets: it is a title, Jesus's name for himself (m3), and it is not put under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mange et boit" (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the participles into a clause, so French needs a subject pronoun the English lacks, and it carries the capital-pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m3), as in John; never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Mwangalieni, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English Readable "Look at him" takes the setting; Swahili carries "him" in the verb (-m-), which cannot take a capital.

decisions.choice: "người này" (B), "ông ta" (R) in the critics' words, with no setting span
decisions.reason: The style guide has opponents speak of Jesus as "ông ta" or "người này"; where the English Readable has the capital-pronoun setting, Vietnamese uses a word that gives him no honour, as the speakers do not.

decisions.choice: "kẻ ham ăn và nghiện rượu" (L); "ham ăn mê uống" (B); "ăn quá nhiều và uống rượu quá nhiều" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision hears the charge against a rebellious son in Deuteronomy 21:20; Literal keeps two nouns of blame, Balanced uses the set phrase for greed at table, and Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "인자" at every level; the critics speak of Jesus with no honorific ("사람이다", "저 사람")
decisions.reason: The speakers mean an insult, so their words give him no honorific, as in Mark 3:21-22 in Korean. "인자" is the title used through the Gospels.

decisions.choice: "ሆዳምና ሰካራም" (a glutton and a drunkard)
decisions.reason: "ሆዳም" and "ሰካራም" are the everyday Amharic insults for one who overeats and one who drinks too much, which is the force of the two Greek words, as in Matthew 11:19.

source.text: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And was justified the wisdom by all the children of her.

en.L: And wisdom was justified by all her children."
en.B: Yet wisdom is shown to be right by all who are her children."
en.R: But God's wisdom is shown to be right by all the people who accept it."

es.L: Y la sabiduría fue reivindicada por todos sus hijos».
es.B: Pero todos los hijos de la sabiduría demuestran que ella tiene razón».
es.R: Pero todas las personas que aceptan la sabiduría de Dios muestran que esa sabiduría tiene razón».

fr.L: Et la sagesse a été justifiée par tous ses enfants. »
fr.B: Pourtant, tous les enfants de la sagesse montrent qu’elle a raison. »
fr.R: Mais tous ceux qui acceptent la sagesse de Dieu montrent qu’elle a raison. »

sw.L: Na hekima ilionyeshwa kuwa sahihi na watoto wake wote."
sw.B: Lakini hekima inaonyeshwa kuwa sahihi na wote walio watoto wake."
sw.R: Lakini watu wote wanaoikubali hekima ya Mungu wanaonyesha kwamba hekima hiyo ni sahihi."

vi.L: Và sự khôn ngoan được xưng là công chính bởi tất cả con cái của nó."
vi.B: Nhưng sự khôn ngoan được chứng tỏ là đúng qua tất cả những người là con cái của nó."
vi.R: Nhưng sự khôn ngoan của Đức Chúa Trời được chứng tỏ là đúng qua tất cả những người tiếp nhận nó."

ko.L: 그러나 지혜는 자기의 모든 자녀에게서 옳다고 인정받았다."
ko.B: 그러나 지혜가 옳다는 것은 지혜의 모든 자녀가 보여 준다."
ko.R: 그러나 하나님의 지혜를 받아들이는 사람들을 보면, 그 지혜가 옳다는 것을 알 수 있다."

pt.L: E a sabedoria foi justificada por todos os seus filhos."
pt.B: Mas todos os filhos da sabedoria mostram que ela tem razão."
pt.R: Mas todas as pessoas que aceitam a sabedoria de Deus mostram que ela está certa."

am.L: ጥበብም በልጆቿ ሁሉ ጸደቀች።»
am.B: ሆኖም ጥበብ ትክክል መሆኗ በልጆቿ ሁሉ ይታያል።»
am.R: ነገር ግን የእግዚአብሔር ጥበብ ትክክል መሆኗን የሚቀበሏት ሰዎች ሁሉ ያሳያሉ።»

decisions.choice: wisdom: God's wisdom, seen in his plan through John and Jesus
decisions.reason: In Proverbs, wisdom is pictured as a woman who calls people to follow her (Proverbs 8:1-4; 9:1-6). Here she stands for God's wise plan, which sent John and Jesus in different ways (compare 11:49).

decisions.choice: her children: those who accept wisdom and live by it
decisions.reason: In Hebrew speech the children of something share its nature. The children of wisdom are the people who accepted God's call through John and Jesus, like the tax collectors of 7:29.

decisions.choice: was justified: was shown to be right
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 7:29: the people who accepted John's baptism declared God right. The tense is a timeless past: wisdom has been proved right every time.

decisions.choice: is shown to be right
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the verb means here, and use the present, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: God's wisdom; the people who accept it
decisions.reason: Readable names whose wisdom it is and explains "her children".

decisions.choice: fue reivindicada
decisions.reason: Shown to be in the right (meaning decision m3). "Justificada" in Spanish now usually means excused.

decisions.choice: her children as the subject: "tous les enfants de la sagesse montrent qu’elle a raison" (B)
alternatives: la sagesse est reconnue juste par tous ses enfants
decisions.reason: French passives with "par" are heavy; making the children the subject says the same thing (m3) in natural French, in the present, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ilionyeshwa kuwa sahihi (L); inaonyeshwa kuwa sahihi (B); wanaonyesha kwamba ni sahihi (R)
decisions.reason: Shown to be in the right (meaning decision m3). "Kuhesabiwa haki" is the phrase for being made righteous before God, and "haki" is kept for righteousness, so it would point the wrong way here.

decisions.choice: "được xưng là công chính" (L); "được chứng tỏ là đúng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 7:29, rendered the same way at Literal; the meaning decision says shown to be right, which Balanced and Readable say. "nó" for wisdom, since Vietnamese does not personify it as "bà".

decisions.choice: "옳다고 인정받았다" (L), "옳다는 것을 보여 준다" (B, R); "자녀" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The verb means shown to be right (meaning decision), as in 7:29. "자녀" for tekna already includes sons and daughters.

decisions.choice: "ጸደቀች" (was justified) at Literal
decisions.reason: "ጸደቀ" belongs to the same family as "ጽድቅ" and means to be shown to be in the right, the sense of the Greek verb, and it echoes "አጸደቁ" in 7:29; Balanced and Readable say the sense plainly.

source.text: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετ’ αὐτοῦ· καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Φαρισαίου κατεκλίθη.

records.literal_gloss: Was asking then one of him of the Pharisees that he would eat with him; and having entered into the house of the Pharisee he reclined.

en.L: Now one of the Pharisees was asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to eat with him, and entering into the Pharisee's house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reclined [at table].
en.B: One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to a meal with him. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into the Pharisee's house and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table.
en.R: A Pharisee invited Jesus to come and eat with him. So Jesus went to the Pharisee's house and lay down on a couch at the table, as people did for a dinner.

es.L: Y uno de los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaba que comiera con él; y entrando en la casa del fariseo, se reclinó [a la mesa].
es.B: Uno de los fariseos invitó a Jesús a comer con él. Entonces Jesús entró en la casa del fariseo y ocupó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar a la mesa.
es.R: Un fariseo invitó a Jesús a comer con él. Entonces Jesús fue a la casa del fariseo y se recostó junto a la mesa, como se hacía en las cenas.

fr.L: Or un des Pharisiens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} priait de manger avec lui ; et étant entré dans la maison du Pharisien, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’étendit [à table].
fr.B: Un des Pharisiens invita Jésus à manger avec lui. Il entra donc dans la maison du Pharisien et prit place à table.
fr.R: Un Pharisien a invité Jésus à venir manger chez lui. Jésus est donc allé chez le Pharisien et s’est allongé sur un divan près de la table, comme on le faisait pour un repas.

sw.L: Basi mmoja wa Mafarisayo alikuwa akimwomba ale pamoja naye; kisha akaingia nyumbani mwa yule Farisayo, akaegemea [mezani].
sw.B: Mmoja wa Mafarisayo alimkaribisha Yesu kula chakula pamoja naye. Basi Yesu akaingia nyumbani kwa yule Farisayo, akakaa mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} mezani.
sw.R: Farisayo mmoja alimkaribisha Yesu aje kula pamoja naye. Kwa hiyo Yesu alikwenda nyumbani kwa yule Farisayo, akajilaza kwenye kochi karibu na meza, kama watu walivyofanya wakati wa karamu.

vi.L: Bấy giờ có một người Pha-ri-si mời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến ăn với mình; và vào nhà người Pha-ri-si ấy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngả mình [dùng bữa].
vi.B: Có một người Pha-ri-si mời Đức Giê-xu đến dùng bữa với mình. Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào nhà người Pha-ri-si ấy và ngồi vào bàn ăn.
vi.R: Có một người Pha-ri-si mời Đức Giê-xu đến ăn với mình. Vậy Đức Giê-xu đến nhà người Pha-ri-si ấy và ngả mình bên bàn ăn, theo cách người ta dự tiệc thời ấy.

ko.L: 바리새파 사람 가운데 한 사람이 자기와 함께 잡수시자고 그분께 청하였다. 그래서 그분은 그 바리새파 사람의 집에 들어가셔서 [식탁에] 기대어 앉으셨다.
ko.B: 바리새파 사람 하나가 예수께 함께 식사하시자고 청하였다. 예수께서 그 바리새파 사람의 집에 들어가셔서 식탁에 앉으셨다.
ko.R: 어떤 바리새파 사람이 예수께 자기 집에 오셔서 함께 식사를 하시자고 청하였다. 예수께서는 그 바리새파 사람의 집에 가셔서, 잔치 때에 사람들이 하던 대로 식탁 옆에 비스듬히 기대어 앉으셨다.

pt.L: E um dos fariseus {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} pedia que comesse com ele; e, entrando na casa do fariseu, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} se reclinou [à mesa].
pt.B: Um dos fariseus convidou Jesus para uma refeição com ele. Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} entrou na casa do fariseu e tomou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} lugar à mesa.
pt.R: Um fariseu convidou Jesus para comer com ele. Então Jesus foi à casa do fariseu e se recostou num divã junto à mesa, como se fazia num jantar.

am.L: ከፈሪሳውያንም አንዱ ከእርሱ ጋር እንዲበላ ይለምነው ነበር፤ ወደ ፈሪሳዊውም ቤት ገብቶ [በማዕድ] ተቀመጠ።
am.B: ከፈሪሳውያን አንዱ ኢየሱስን ከእርሱ ጋር እንዲበላ ጋበዘው። ስለዚህ ወደ ፈሪሳዊው ቤት ገብቶ በማዕድ ተቀመጠ።
am.R: አንድ ፈሪሳዊ ኢየሱስን ከእርሱ ጋር እንዲበላ ጋበዘው። ስለዚህ ኢየሱስ ወደ ፈሪሳዊው ቤት ሄደ፤ በዚያን ጊዜ ሰዎች ለግብዣ እንደሚያደርጉት በማዕዱ አጠገብ ባለ መደገፊያ ላይ ጋደም አለ።

decisions.choice: reclined: lay on a couch at the table, leaning on one elbow
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on couches around a low table, with their feet away from it. This is why the woman could stand behind Jesus at his feet (7:38).

decisions.choice: a Pharisee's invitation: Jesus ate with Pharisees as well as with sinners
decisions.reason: Luke tells of three meals with Pharisees (7:36; 11:37; 14:1). Jesus has just been called a friend of sinners (7:34).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: lay down on a couch at the table, as people did for a dinner
decisions.reason: Readable explains the custom, which the next verses need.

decisions.choice: se reclinó [a la mesa]
decisions.reason: Guests at a dinner lay on couches around the table (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the reclining, with the table supplied; Readable describes it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: s’étendit [à table] (L); prit place à table (B); s’est allongé sur un divan près de la table (R)
alternatives: se mit à table at every level
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches, leaning on one elbow (m1), which explains how the woman could stand at his feet. Literal keeps the posture; Balanced uses the ordinary phrase; Readable describes the custom, as the English does.

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens, capitalised (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the capital marks the name of the movement (m4 at 7:30).

decisions.choice: akaegemea [mezani] (reclined [at table])
decisions.reason: Guests at a dinner lay on couches around the table (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the reclining, with the table supplied; Readable describes it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ngả mình [dùng bữa]" (L); "ngồi vào bàn ăn" (B); "ngả mình bên bàn ăn, theo cách người ta dự tiệc thời ấy" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 2:15 and Luke 5:29: guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision); Literal shows the posture, Balanced uses the ordinary words, and Readable explains it, as the English Readable does. The posture matters for 7:38, where the woman stands behind him at his feet.

decisions.choice: "[식탁에] 기대어 앉다" (L); "식탁에 앉다" (B); "비스듬히 기대어 앉다" with an explanation (R), here and in 7:37 and 7:49
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches, leaning on one elbow (meaning decision); Literal keeps the posture, as in Luke 5:29 in Korean, and Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "[በማዕድ] ተቀመጠ" (sat [at table]) for "reclined"
decisions.reason: Amharic has no verb for reclining at a meal; "to sit at the table" says what the Greek means, as in Matthew 8:11, and Literal brackets the words for the table. Readable describes the custom, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἁμαρτωλός, καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου, κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου καὶ στᾶσα ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ κλαίουσα, τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν, καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And look a woman who was in the city a sinner, and having learned that he is reclining in the house of the Pharisee, having brought an alabaster flask of perfume \v 38 and having stood behind at the feet of him weeping, with the tears she began to wet the feet of him and with the hairs of the head of her she was wiping, and was kissing the feet of him and was anointing with the perfume.

en.L: And look, a woman in the town who was a sinner, learning that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table] in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster flask of perfume, \v 38 and standing behind at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, weeping, she began to wet {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with [her] tears, and she was wiping [them] with the hair of her head, and she was kissing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and anointing [them] with the perfume.
en.B: Now there was a woman in the town who was a sinner. When she found out that Jesus was at table in the Pharisee's house, she came with an alabaster flask of perfume. \v 38 She stood behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, crying, and began to wet {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with her tears. She dried them with the hair of her head, and she kissed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet over and over and anointed them with the perfume.
en.R: In that town there was a woman everyone knew as a sinner. She heard that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee's house. So she came, carrying a beautiful stone jar full of expensive perfume. \v 38 She stood behind Jesus at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and she was crying. Her tears fell on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and made them wet. Then she dried {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with her hair. She kept kissing them and pouring the perfume on them.

es.L: Y mira, una mujer que en la ciudad era pecadora, al saber que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba reclinado [a la mesa] en la casa del fariseo, trajo un frasco de alabastro con perfume, \v 38 y poniéndose detrás, junto a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, llorando, comenzó a mojar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies con [sus] lágrimas, y [los] secaba con los cabellos de su cabeza, y besaba {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies y [los] ungía con el perfume.
es.B: Había en el pueblo una mujer que era pecadora. Cuando supo que Jesús estaba a la mesa en la casa del fariseo, llegó con un frasco de alabastro lleno de perfume. \v 38 Se puso detrás de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, llorando, y comenzó a mojar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies con sus lágrimas. Los secaba con los cabellos de su cabeza, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} besaba los pies una y otra vez y los ungía con el perfume.
es.R: En aquel pueblo había una mujer a la que todos conocían como pecadora. Ella oyó que Jesús estaba comiendo en la casa del fariseo. Así que fue allá con un hermoso frasco de piedra lleno de un perfume caro. \v 38 Se puso detrás de Jesús, junto a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, y lloraba. Las lágrimas de ella caían sobre {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies y los mojaban. Después {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} secó los pies con su cabello. No dejaba de besarlos y de derramar el perfume sobre ellos.

fr.L: Et voici, une femme qui était dans la ville une pécheresse, ayant appris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était à table dans la maison du Pharisien, apporta un flacon d’albâtre [plein] de parfum, \v 38 et se tenant derrière, à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, en pleurant, elle se mit à mouiller {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds de [ses] larmes, et elle [les] essuyait avec les cheveux de sa tête, et elle embrassait {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds et [les] oignait du parfum.
fr.B: Or il y avait dans la ville une femme qui était une pécheresse. Quand elle apprit que Jésus était à table dans la maison du Pharisien, elle vint avec un flacon d’albâtre rempli de parfum. \v 38 Elle se tint derrière {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, en pleurant, et se mit à mouiller {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds de ses larmes. Elle les essuyait avec ses cheveux, elle couvrait {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds de baisers et les oignait de parfum.
fr.R: Dans cette ville, il y avait une femme que tout le monde connaissait comme une pécheresse. Elle a appris que Jésus mangeait chez le Pharisien. Alors elle est venue avec un beau vase de pierre plein d’un parfum très cher. \v 38 Elle s’est tenue derrière Jésus, à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, et elle pleurait. Ses larmes tombaient sur les pieds de Jésus et les mouillaient. Puis elle a essuyé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds avec ses cheveux. Elle n’arrêtait pas de les embrasser et de verser le parfum dessus.

sw.L: Na tazama, mwanamke mmoja aliyekuwa mwenye dhambi katika mji ule, alipojua kwamba anaegemea [mezani] nyumbani mwa yule Farisayo, alileta chupa ya alabasta yenye manukato, \v 38 akasimama nyuma karibu na miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} akilia, akaanza kuilowesha miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa machozi, akawa akiipangusa kwa nywele za kichwa chake, akiibusu miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kuipaka manukato.
sw.B: Basi kulikuwa na mwanamke mmoja katika mji ule ambaye alikuwa mwenye dhambi. Alipojua kwamba Yesu alikuwa mezani nyumbani mwa yule Farisayo, alikuja na chupa ya alabasta yenye manukato. \v 38 Akasimama nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, karibu na miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akilia, akaanza kuilowesha miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa machozi yake. Akaipangusa kwa nywele za kichwa chake, akaibusu miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tena na tena, akaipaka manukato.
sw.R: Katika mji ule kulikuwa na mwanamke ambaye kila mtu alimjua kuwa mwenye dhambi. Alisikia kwamba Yesu alikuwa akila nyumbani kwa yule Farisayo. Kwa hiyo akaja, amebeba chupa nzuri ya jiwe iliyojaa manukato ya bei ghali. \v 38 Akasimama nyuma ya Yesu karibu na miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, naye alikuwa akilia. Machozi yake yakadondoka juu ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kuilowesha. Kisha akaipangusa miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa nywele zake. Akaendelea kuibusu na kuimwagia manukato.

vi.L: Và kìa, một người đàn bà trong thành là người tội lỗi, biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ngả mình [dùng bữa] trong nhà người Pha-ri-si, đem đến một bình thạch cao đựng dầu thơm, \v 38 và đứng phía sau, nơi chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vừa khóc, bà bắt đầu lấy nước mắt làm ướt chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rồi lấy tóc trên đầu mình mà lau, và hôn chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và xức dầu thơm [cho chân ấy].
vi.B: Trong thành có một người phụ nữ nổi tiếng là tội lỗi. Khi biết Đức Giê-xu đang dùng bữa trong nhà người Pha-ri-si, bà đem đến một bình thạch cao đựng dầu thơm. \v 38 Bà đứng phía sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nơi chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vừa khóc vừa để nước mắt làm ướt chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Bà lấy tóc mình lau chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, hôn chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mãi, và xức dầu thơm cho chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Trong thị trấn ấy có một người phụ nữ mà ai cũng biết là người tội lỗi. Bà nghe tin Đức Giê-xu đang dùng bữa tại nhà người Pha-ri-si. Vì vậy bà đến, mang theo một bình đá đẹp đựng dầu thơm đắt tiền. \v 38 Bà đứng phía sau Đức Giê-xu, nơi chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và bà khóc. Nước mắt bà rơi xuống làm ướt chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Rồi bà lấy tóc mình lau khô chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Bà cứ hôn chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và đổ dầu thơm lên chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 보라, 그 고을에 죄인인 한 여자가 있었는데, 그분이 그 바리새파 사람의 집에서 [식탁에] 기대어 앉아 계시다는 것을 알고, 향유가 든 설화석고 병을 가지고 와서 \v 38 뒤에서 그분의 발 곁에 서서 울며, 눈물로 그분의 발을 적시기 시작하였다. 그리고 자기 머리카락으로 [그 발을] 닦고, 그분의 발에 입을 맞추며 향유를 발라 드렸다.
ko.B: 그 고을에 죄인으로 알려진 여자가 하나 있었다. 그 여자는 예수께서 그 바리새파 사람의 집에서 식사하고 계시다는 것을 알고, 향유가 든 설화석고 병을 가지고 왔다. \v 38 그리고 예수의 뒤쪽 발치에 서서 울며, 눈물로 예수의 발을 적시기 시작하였다. 그 여자는 자기 머리카락으로 그 발을 닦고, 그 발에 거듭 입을 맞추며 향유를 발라 드렸다.
ko.R: 그 마을에 모두가 죄인으로 알고 있는 여자가 하나 있었다. 그 여자는 예수께서 그 바리새파 사람의 집에서 식사하고 계시다는 소식을 들었다. 그래서 하얀 돌로 만든 아름다운 병에 비싼 향유를 가득 담아 가지고 왔다. \v 38 그 여자는 예수의 뒤쪽 발치에 서서 울었다. 눈물이 예수의 발에 떨어져 발이 젖었다. 그 여자는 자기 머리카락으로 예수의 발을 닦았다. 그리고 그 발에 계속 입을 맞추며 향유를 발라 드렸다.

pt.L: E eis que uma mulher que era pecadora na cidade, sabendo que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava reclinado [à mesa] na casa do fariseu, trouxe um frasco de alabastro com perfume \v 38 e, pondo-se atrás, junto aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés, chorando, começou a molhar os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés com as lágrimas e os enxugava com os cabelos da cabeça dela, e beijava os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés e [os] ungia com o perfume.
pt.B: Havia na cidade uma mulher que era pecadora. Quando soube que Jesus estava à mesa na casa do fariseu, ela foi até lá com um frasco de alabastro cheio de perfume. \v 38 Ficou atrás {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, junto aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés, chorando, e começou a molhar os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés com as lágrimas. Ela os enxugava com os próprios cabelos, beijava os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés sem parar e os ungia com o perfume.
pt.R: Naquela cidade havia uma mulher que todos conheciam como pecadora. Ela soube que Jesus estava comendo na casa do fariseu. Então ela foi até lá, levando um lindo vaso de pedra cheio de perfume caro. \v 38 Ela ficou atrás de Jesus, junto aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés, e estava chorando. As lágrimas dela caíam nos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés e os molhavam. Depois ela enxugou os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés com os cabelos. Ela continuava beijando os pés de Jesus e derramando o perfume neles.

am.L: እነሆም፣ በከተማዪቱ ኃጢአተኛ የነበረች አንዲት ሴት በፈሪሳዊው ቤት [በማዕድ] ተቀምጦ እንዳለ ባወቀች ጊዜ፣ የሽቱ የአልባስጥሮስ ብልቃጥ አመጣች፤ \v 38 እያለቀሰችም ከበስተ ኋላው በእግሩ አጠገብ ቆማ እግሩን በእንባዋ ማራስ ጀመረች፤ በራሷ ፀጉርም ታብሰው ነበር፤ እግሩንም ትስመው ነበር፤ በሽቱውም ትቀባው ነበር።
am.B: በዚያች ከተማ ኃጢአተኛ የሆነች አንዲት ሴት ነበረች። ኢየሱስ በፈሪሳዊው ቤት በማዕድ መቀመጡን ባወቀች ጊዜ ሽቱ የሞላበት የአልባስጥሮስ ብልቃጥ ይዛ መጣች። \v 38 ከኋላው በእግሩ አጠገብ ቆማ እያለቀሰች እግሩን በእንባዋ ማራስ ጀመረች። በራሷ ፀጉርም አበሰችው፤ እግሩንም ደጋግማ ሳመችው፤ ሽቱውንም ቀባችው።
am.R: በዚያች ከተማ ሰው ሁሉ ኃጢአተኛ መሆኗን የሚያውቃት አንዲት ሴት ነበረች። እርሷም ኢየሱስ በፈሪሳዊው ቤት እየበላ መሆኑን ሰማች። ስለዚህ ውድ ሽቱ የሞላበት ያማረ የድንጋይ ብልቃጥ ይዛ መጣች። \v 38 ከኢየሱስ ኋላ በእግሩ አጠገብ ቆማ ታለቅስ ነበር። እንባዋ በእግሩ ላይ ወድቆ አራሰው። ከዚያም እግሩን በፀጉሯ አበሰች። እግሩን ደጋግማ ትስም ነበር፤ ሽቱውንም በእግሩ ላይ ታፈስ ነበር።

decisions.choice: a sinner: a woman known in the town for an immoral life
alternatives: a woman who had committed some private sin
decisions.reason: The word marks someone whose way of life openly broke God's law (5:30). Luke does not say what her sin was. Later tradition made her Mary Magdalene, but Luke introduces Mary Magdalene in the next chapter as a different person (8:2).

decisions.choice: an alabaster flask of perfume: a sealed jar of soft stone holding costly perfumed oil
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a smooth, pale stone used for jars of precious perfume. The perfume was far more costly than the olive oil of 7:46.

decisions.choice: wiping his feet with her hair: an act of humble devotion, unusual in public
decisions.reason: A respectable woman did not let down her hair in front of men. She uses her own hair and tears where the host had given no water (7:44).

decisions.choice: this is not the anointing at Bethany
alternatives: the same event as Mark 14:3-9 and John 12:1-8
decisions.reason: Those Gospels tell of a woman who anointed Jesus at Bethany, near Jerusalem, in the last week of his life. Luke's story takes place in Galilee, in a Pharisee's house, much earlier. Luke does not tell the Bethany anointing.

decisions.choice: began to wet, was kissing, was anointing: actions continued over time
decisions.reason: The tenses describe what she kept on doing. Jesus says she has not stopped kissing his feet (7:45).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: a beautiful stone jar
decisions.reason: Readable describes alabaster instead of naming it.

decisions.choice: anointed (B); pouring the perfume on (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing the feet meant.

decisions.choice: une pécheresse
decisions.reason: French has a feminine form of "pécheur", so it keeps the same word as in "les pécheurs" (7:34), at every level. The meaning decision says that she was known for an immoral life; "prostituée" would say more than the text does.

decisions.choice: imperfects "essuyait", "couvrait … de baisers", "oignait" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek verbs describe actions that went on over time (m5); the French imperfect says that within passé simple narration, where English Balanced adds "over and over".

decisions.choice: "bà" for the woman (7:37-50 in the narrative), "chị ấy" in Jesus' words to Simon, and "con" when Jesus speaks to her
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose a word that says something of age and relation. Luke gives no age; "bà" is the neutral respectful word for a grown woman in narrative; Jesus speaks of her to Simon as "chị ấy", a plain courteous word between them, and to her as "con", as he does to the woman in Mark 5:34.

decisions.choice: "bình thạch cao đựng dầu thơm" (L, B); "bình đá đẹp đựng dầu thơm đắt tiền" (R)
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a soft stone (meaning decision), which "thạch cao" names; "dầu thơm" as in John 12:3. Readable describes it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "설화석고 병" (L, B), "하얀 돌로 만든 아름다운 병" (R); "향유"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 14:3 in Korean: "옥합" is the familiar word of older versions but means a jade box; the flask was of alabaster, a soft stone (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "향유를 발라 드렸다" with the honorific "드리다"
decisions.reason: The narrator honours Jesus in what is done to him, as in John 11:2 and 12:3 in Korean ("닦아 드리다").

decisions.choice: "እግሩ" (his foot) for "his feet"
decisions.reason: Amharic normally uses the singular "እግር" for both feet of a person, and "እግሮቹ" would sound as though they were counted; the sense is the same.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Οὗτος εἰ ἦν προφήτης, ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the Pharisee the [one] having invited him spoke within himself saying, This [man] if he were a prophet, would know who and what kind the woman who is touching him, that a sinner she is.

en.L: Now when the Pharisee who had invited {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw [this], he spoke within himself, saying, "This man, if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a prophet, would know who and what sort of woman [this is] who is touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, that she is a sinner."
en.B: The Pharisee who had invited {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw this and said to himself, "This man, if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a prophet, would have known who this woman is who is touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and what sort of woman she is: a sinner."
en.R: The Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw what was happening. He thought, "This man cannot be a prophet. A prophet would know who this woman is, the one touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He would know what kind of woman she is. She is a sinner!"

es.L: Y al ver [esto] el fariseo que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había invitado, dijo dentro de sí: «Este, si fuera profeta, sabría quién y qué clase de mujer [es] la que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} está tocando, que es una pecadora».
es.B: El fariseo que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había invitado vio esto y se dijo: «Si este hombre fuera profeta, sabría quién es esta mujer que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} toca, y qué clase de mujer es: una pecadora».
es.R: El fariseo que había invitado a Jesús vio lo que pasaba. Pensó: «Este hombre no puede ser profeta. Un profeta sabría quién es esta mujer que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} está tocando. Sabría qué clase de mujer es. ¡Es una pecadora!».

fr.L: Or, voyant [cela], le Pharisien qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait invité se dit en lui-même : « Celui-ci, s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était prophète, saurait qui et quelle sorte de femme [est celle] qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} touche : que c’est une pécheresse. »
fr.B: Voyant cela, le Pharisien qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait invité se dit : « Si cet homme était un prophète, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} saurait qui est cette femme qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} touche, et quelle sorte de femme elle est : une pécheresse. »
fr.R: Le Pharisien qui avait invité Jésus a vu ce qui se passait. Il a pensé : « Cet homme ne peut pas être un prophète. Un prophète saurait qui est cette femme, celle qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} touche. Il saurait quel genre de femme elle est. C’est une pécheresse ! »

sw.L: Basi yule Farisayo aliyemwalika alipoona [hayo], alinena ndani yake, akisema, "Huyu, kama angekuwa nabii, angejua ni nani, na ni mwanamke wa namna gani huyu anayemgusa, kwamba ni mwenye dhambi."
sw.B: Yule Farisayo aliyemwalika alipoona hayo, alisema moyoni, "Kama mtu huyu angekuwa nabii, angejua mwanamke huyu anayemgusa ni nani, na ni wa namna gani: ni mwenye dhambi."
sw.R: Yule Farisayo aliyemwalika Yesu aliona yaliyokuwa yakitokea. Akawaza, "Mtu huyu hawezi kuwa nabii. Nabii angejua mwanamke huyu anayemgusa ni nani. Angejua ni mwanamke wa namna gani. Ni mwenye dhambi!"

vi.L: Thấy [vậy], người Pha-ri-si đã mời Đức Giê-xu nói thầm trong lòng: "Người này nếu là nhà tiên tri, thì đã biết người đàn bà đang chạm vào mình là ai và là hạng người nào, vì bà ấy là người tội lỗi."
vi.B: Người Pha-ri-si đã mời Đức Giê-xu thấy vậy thì nghĩ thầm: "Nếu ông này là nhà tiên tri, hẳn ông ấy đã biết người đàn bà đang chạm vào mình là ai và là loại người gì: bà ta là người tội lỗi!"
vi.R: Người Pha-ri-si đã mời Đức Giê-xu thấy chuyện đang xảy ra. Ông nghĩ thầm: "Người này không thể là nhà tiên tri. Nếu là nhà tiên tri, ông ta đã biết người đàn bà đang chạm vào mình là ai. Ông ta đã biết bà ấy là hạng người nào. Bà ấy là người tội lỗi!"

ko.L: 그분을 초대한 바리새파 사람이 [이것을] 보고 속으로 말했다. "이 사람이 예언자라면, 자기를 만지고 있는 이 여자가 누구이며 어떤 여자인지, 곧 죄인이라는 것을 알았을 것이다."
ko.B: 예수를 초대한 바리새파 사람이 이것을 보고 속으로 말했다. "이 사람이 정말 예언자라면, 자기를 만지는 이 여자가 누구이고 어떤 여자인지 알았을 것이다. 이 여자는 죄인이다."
ko.R: 예수를 초대한 바리새파 사람이 이 모습을 보았다. 그는 속으로 생각했다. "이 사람은 예언자일 리가 없다. 예언자라면 자기를 만지는 이 여자가 누구인지 알 것이다. 어떤 여자인지도 알 것이다. 이 여자는 죄인이 아닌가!"

pt.L: Mas, vendo [isso], o fariseu que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} tinha convidado disse consigo mesmo: "Este [homem], se fosse profeta, saberia quem e que tipo de mulher [é esta] que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} está tocando, que ela é uma pecadora."
pt.B: O fariseu que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} tinha convidado viu isso e disse consigo mesmo: "Se este homem fosse profeta, saberia quem é esta mulher que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} está tocando e que tipo de mulher ela é: uma pecadora."
pt.R: O fariseu que tinha convidado Jesus viu o que estava acontecendo. Ele pensou: "Este homem não pode ser profeta. Um profeta saberia quem é esta mulher que está tocando {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}. Saberia que tipo de mulher ela é. Ela é uma pecadora!"

am.L: የጋበዘውም ፈሪሳዊ [ይህን] አይቶ በልቡ እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህ ሰው ነቢይ ቢሆን ኖሮ፣ የምትነካው ሴት ማን እንደ ሆነችና ምን ዓይነት ሴት እንደ ሆነች፣ ኃጢአተኛ እንደ ሆነች ባወቀ ነበር።»
am.B: የጋበዘውም ፈሪሳዊ ይህን አይቶ በልቡ እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህ ሰው ነቢይ ቢሆን ኖሮ፣ የምትነካው ይህች ሴት ማን እንደ ሆነችና ምን ዓይነት ሴት እንደ ሆነች ባወቀ ነበር፤ ኃጢአተኛ ናት።»
am.R: ኢየሱስን የጋበዘው ፈሪሳዊ የሆነውን ነገር አየ። እንዲህም ብሎ አሰበ፦ «ይህ ሰው ነቢይ ሊሆን አይችልም። ነቢይ ቢሆን ኖሮ የምትነካው ሴት ማን እንደ ሆነች ያውቅ ነበር። ምን ዓይነት ሴት እንደ ሆነችም ያውቅ ነበር። እርሷ ኃጢአተኛ ናት!»

decisions.choice: if he were a prophet, he would know: the Pharisee assumes that Jesus is not a prophet
alternatives: a real question whether he is
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence states something contrary to fact: he would know, but he does not, so he is no prophet. Jesus answers by reading the Pharisee's own unspoken thoughts (7:40).

decisions.choice: a prophet, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the prophet, the reading of some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts have "the prophet", meaning the prophet like Moses promised in Deuteronomy 18:15. Most have "a prophet". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: touching: the touch of a sinner would make him unclean, in the Pharisee's eyes
decisions.reason: The Pharisees took great care to avoid what made them unclean. The host thinks Jesus should have known and drawn back.

decisions.choice: spoke within himself: thought to himself, without speaking aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase means private thought (3:8; 12:17).

decisions.choice: This man cannot be a prophet. A prophet would know
alternatives: if he were a prophet, he would know
decisions.reason: Readable states the conclusion the condition implies, as the meaning decision explains, and then gives the reasoning.

decisions.choice: "người này" (L), "ông này" (B), "ông ta" (R) for Jesus in the Pharisee's thoughts, with no setting span; "mình" for "him"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the Pharisee assumes Jesus is not a prophet; he speaks of him without honour, as the style guide sets for those who doubt him, so the English capital-pronoun spans have no counterpart here.

decisions.choice: The Pharisee thinks of Jesus as "이 사람" with no honorific
decisions.reason: He assumes that Jesus is not a prophet (meaning decision); giving Jesus honorifics in his thoughts would misrepresent them. The narrator still honours Jesus.

decisions.choice: "በልቡ እንዲህ አለ" (he said in his heart)
decisions.reason: Amharic speaks of thinking as saying something in one's heart, which gives the Greek "spoke within himself" exactly: he did not speak aloud.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σίμων, ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And answering Jesus said to him, Simon, I have to you something to say.

en.L: And answering, Jesus said to him, "Simon, I have something to say to you."
en.B: Jesus answered him, "Simon, there is something I want to tell you."
en.R: Jesus answered the Pharisee's thoughts. He said, "Simon, I have something to tell you."

es.L: Y respondiendo, Jesús le dijo: «Simón, tengo algo que decirte».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Simón, hay algo que quiero decirte».
es.R: Jesús respondió a lo que el fariseo estaba pensando. Le dijo: «Simón, tengo algo que decirte».

fr.L: Et prenant la parole, Jésus lui dit : « Simon, j’ai quelque chose à te dire. »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Simon, il y a une chose que je voudrais te dire. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu à ce que pensait le Pharisien. Il a dit : « Simon, j’ai quelque chose à te dire. »

sw.L: Naye Yesu akajibu, akamwambia, "Simoni, nina neno la kukuambia."
sw.B: Yesu alimjibu, "Simoni, kuna jambo nataka kukuambia."
sw.R: Yesu aliyajibu mawazo ya yule Farisayo. Akasema, "Simoni, nina jambo la kukuambia."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu đáp lại, nói với ông: "Si-môn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có điều muốn nói với ông."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp lời ông: "Si-môn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có điều muốn nói với ông."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời ý nghĩ của người Pha-ri-si. Ngài nói: "Si-môn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có điều muốn nói với ông."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 대답하여 그에게 말씀하셨다. "시몬아, 내가 너에게 할 말이 있다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "시몬아, 너에게 해 줄 말이 있다."
ko.R: 예수께서는 그 바리새파 사람의 속마음에 대답하셨다. 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "시몬아, 너에게 할 말이 있다."

pt.L: E, respondendo, Jesus lhe disse: "Simão, tenho uma coisa para lhe dizer."
pt.B: Jesus lhe respondeu: "Simão, há uma coisa que eu quero lhe dizer."
pt.R: Jesus respondeu ao que o fariseu estava pensando. Ele disse: "Simão, tenho uma coisa para dizer a você."

am.L: ኢየሱስም መልሶ «ስምዖን ሆይ፣ የምነግርህ ነገር አለኝ» አለው።
am.B: ኢየሱስም «ስምዖን፣ የምነግርህ አንድ ነገር አለ» ብሎ መለሰለት።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ፈሪሳዊው በልቡ ላሰበው ነገር መልስ ሰጠ። እንዲህም አለው፦ «ስምዖን፣ የምነግርህ ነገር አለኝ።»

decisions.choice: answering: Jesus answers what the Pharisee only thought
decisions.reason: The host spoke only within himself (7:39). Jesus answers him, which shows that he is indeed a prophet who knows hearts (5:22; 6:8).

decisions.choice: Simon: the Pharisee's name
decisions.reason: Simon was a common name. This Simon is the Pharisee who invited Jesus, not the disciple Simon Peter.

decisions.choice: answered the Pharisee's thoughts
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus answered, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls Simon "ông" (7:40-47)
decisions.reason: Simon is a grown man and Jesus' host; "ông" is the polite word for him, as Jesus speaks to the centurion in Matthew 8:13.

source.text: ὁ δέ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπέ, φησίν.

records.literal_gloss: And he: Teacher, say [it], he says.

en.L: And he says, "Teacher, say [it]."
en.B: "Say it, Teacher," he replied.
en.R: Simon said, "Tell me, Teacher."

es.L: Y él dice: «Maestro, dilo».
es.B: «Dilo, Maestro», respondió él.
es.R: Simón dijo: «Dime, Maestro».

fr.L: Et lui : « Maître, dis[-le] », dit-il.
fr.B: « Parle, Maître », répondit-il.
fr.R: Simon a dit : « Dis-moi, Maître. »

sw.L: Naye anasema, "Mwalimu, sema."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Sema, Mwalimu."
sw.R: Simoni akasema, "Niambie, Mwalimu."

vi.L: Và ông nói: "Thưa Thầy, xin cứ nói."
vi.B: Ông đáp: "Thưa Thầy, xin Thầy cứ nói."
vi.R: Si-môn nói: "Thưa Thầy, xin Thầy nói đi."

ko.L: 그러자 그가 말한다. "선생님, 말씀하십시오."
ko.B: 시몬이 대답했다. "선생님, 말씀하십시오."
ko.R: 시몬이 말했다. "선생님, 말씀해 보십시오."

pt.L: E ele diz: "Mestre, dize."
pt.B: "Fala, Mestre", respondeu ele.
pt.R: Simão disse: "Fala, Mestre."

am.L: እርሱም «መምህር ሆይ፣ ተናገር» ይላል።
am.B: እርሱም «መምህር ሆይ፣ ተናገር» ብሎ መለሰ።
am.R: ስምዖንም «መምህር ሆይ፣ ንገረኝ» አለ።

decisions.choice: Teacher: a respectful title for a teacher of the law
decisions.reason: Simon gives Jesus the title of a respected teacher (3:12), not more.

decisions.choice: he says: a present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Greek often tells a past event in the present for vividness.

decisions.choice: replied (B); said (R)
decisions.reason: English tells the story in the past.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); past at Balanced and Readable (respondió, dijo)
decisions.reason: Luke tells this past event in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does.

decisions.choice: Maître for "Teacher" in address at every level (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in Mark: "Maître" is the French way to address a respected teacher; "Enseignant" is a job title and is not used to address someone.

decisions.choice: "dit-il" after the words, as in the Greek (L)
decisions.reason: Luke's historic present stands after the words, as a French incise does; with "dire" the present and the passé simple are the same form.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anasema); past at Balanced and Readable (akajibu, akasema)
decisions.reason: Luke tells this past event in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past.

decisions.choice: "Thưa Thầy" for "Teacher"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says a respectful title for a teacher of the law; "Thầy" says exactly that, and here Simon uses it as a host's courtesy. Literal leaves out "đã" for the historic present "he says", as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: "선생님" for didaskale; Simon speaks in 합쇼체; "말한다" (L) for the present tense
decisions.reason: "선생님" is the respectful address for a teacher (meaning decision) and the word of Mark in Korean; the host speaks politely to his guest even while he doubts him. Literal keeps Luke's historic present, as Mark's Literal does in Korean.

decisions.choice: "ይላል" (he says) at Literal
decisions.reason: The Greek tells the story here with a present tense; Literal keeps it with the Amharic present "ይላል", as the style guide asks, and the other levels use the past.

source.text: δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι· ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα.

records.literal_gloss: Two debtors were to a moneylender certain; the one owed denarii five hundred, the and other fifty.

en.L: "Two debtors belonged to a certain moneylender; the one owed 500 denarii, and the other fifty.
en.B: Jesus said, "A moneylender had two men who owed him money. One owed him 500 denarii, and the other fifty.
en.R: Jesus said, "Two men owed money to a man who lent money. One of them owed him 500 silver coins. The other owed him fifty.

es.L: «Dos deudores tenía cierto prestamista; uno le debía quinientos denarios, y el otro cincuenta.
es.B: Jesús dijo: «Un prestamista tenía dos hombres que le debían dinero. Uno le debía quinientos denarios, y el otro cincuenta.
es.R: Jesús dijo: «Dos hombres le debían dinero a un hombre que prestaba dinero. Uno de ellos le debía quinientas monedas de plata. El otro le debía cincuenta.

fr.L: « Un prêteur avait deux débiteurs ; l’un devait 500 deniers, et l’autre cinquante.
fr.B: Jésus dit : « Un prêteur avait deux hommes qui lui devaient de l’argent. L’un lui devait 500 deniers, l’autre cinquante.
fr.R: Jésus a dit : « Deux hommes avaient emprunté de l’argent au même prêteur. L’un lui devait 500 pièces d’argent. L’autre lui en devait cinquante.

sw.L: "Wadeni wawili walikuwa na mkopeshaji fulani; mmoja alidaiwa dinari mia tano, na yule mwingine hamsini.
sw.B: Yesu alisema, "Mkopeshaji mmoja alikuwa na watu wawili waliokuwa na deni lake. Mmoja alikuwa anadaiwa dinari mia tano, na mwingine hamsini.
sw.R: Yesu alisema, "Watu wawili walikuwa wanadaiwa fedha na mtu mmoja aliyekopesha fedha. Mmoja wao alidaiwa sarafu mia tano za fedha. Yule mwingine alidaiwa hamsini.

vi.L: "Một người cho vay kia có hai con nợ; một người nợ năm trăm đơ-ni-ê, còn người kia năm mươi.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Có một người cho vay có hai con nợ. Một người nợ ông năm trăm đơ-ni-ê, người kia nợ năm mươi.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Có hai người nợ tiền một người cho vay. Một người nợ ông năm trăm đồng bạc. Người kia nợ ông năm mươi đồng.

ko.L: "어떤 채권자에게 빚진 사람이 둘 있었다. 한 사람은 오백 데나리온을, 다른 사람은 오십 [데나리온을] 빚졌다.
ko.B: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "돈을 빌려주는 어떤 사람에게 빚진 사람이 둘 있었다. 한 사람은 오백 데나리온을 빚졌고, 다른 사람은 오십 데나리온을 빚졌다.
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "돈을 빌려주는 사람에게 돈을 빌린 사람이 둘 있었다. 한 사람은 은돈 오백 닢을 빚졌고, 다른 사람은 은돈 오십 닢을 빚졌다.

pt.L: "Um certo credor tinha dois devedores: um devia quinhentos denários, e o outro, cinquenta.
pt.B: Jesus disse: "Um homem que emprestava dinheiro tinha dois devedores. Um lhe devia quinhentos denários, e o outro, cinquenta.
pt.R: Jesus disse: "Dois homens deviam dinheiro a um homem que fazia empréstimos. Um deles devia a ele quinhentas moedas de prata. O outro devia cinquenta.

am.L: «አንድ አበዳሪ ሁለት ባለ ዕዳዎች ነበሩት፤ አንዱ 500 ዲናር ዕዳ ነበረበት፤ ሌላውም ሃምሳ።
am.B: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አለ፦ «አንድ አበዳሪ ገንዘብ የተበደሩት ሁለት ሰዎች ነበሩ። አንዱ 500 ዲናር ዕዳ ነበረበት፤ ሌላው ደግሞ ሃምሳ።
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አለ፦ «ሁለት ሰዎች ገንዘብ ከሚያበድር ሰው ተበድረው ነበር። አንዱ 500 የብር ሳንቲም ዕዳ ነበረበት። ሌላው ደግሞ ሃምሳ የብር ሳንቲም ዕዳ ነበረበት።

decisions.choice: denarii: Roman silver coins, each the usual pay for a day's work
decisions.reason: A denarius was a laborer's wage for a day (Matthew 20:2). So 500 denarii was more than a year's wages, and fifty about two months' wages. Both were real debts; one was ten times the other.

decisions.choice: a story told to answer Simon's thoughts
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the unspoken charge of 7:39 with a short parable.

decisions.choice: Jesus said
decisions.reason: The Greek starts the story without a new speech verb. Balanced and Readable name the speaker after Simon's reply; Literal only opens the quotation.

decisions.choice: silver coins (R); denarii (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the coin instead of naming it. A modern sum would be misleading, since wages differ from place to place; the meaning decision gives the coin's worth.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:42
decisions.reason: The parable and its question are one speech.

decisions.choice: denarios (L, B); monedas de plata (R), with no units span
alternatives: a units span giving the sums in wages
decisions.reason: The English names the coin here (meaning decision m1) and has no units span, so Spanish has none either; Readable says "monedas de plata" as the English Readable says "silver coins".

decisions.choice: 500 deniers (L, B); 500 pièces d’argent (R), in figures
decisions.reason: "Denier" is the usual French name for the Roman coin. The style guide writes numbers above "cent" in figures, so "500" but "cinquante".

decisions.choice: dinari (L, B); sarafu za fedha (R), with no units span
alternatives: a units span giving the sums in wages
decisions.reason: The English names the coin here (meaning decision m1) and has no units span, so Swahili has none either; Readable says "sarafu za fedha" as the English Readable says "silver coins".

decisions.choice: "đơ-ni-ê" (L, B); "đồng bạc" (R) for denarii
decisions.reason: As in John 6:7 and 12:5 for the coin's name; Readable says what the coins were, as the English Readable does. Numbers are written in words in running text, as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: "데나리온" (L, B); "은돈 ... 닢" (R); no units span
alternatives: a units setting with a modern value, as in John 6:7 in Korean
decisions.reason: The English gives the coins with no setting, so Korean does the same: Literal and Balanced keep the name of the coin, as in Mark 12:15 and John 12:5 in Korean, and Readable says silver coins, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ዲናር" (L, B); "የብር ሳንቲም" (silver coins) (R), with no units span
alternatives: a units setting giving the value in wages, as for coins elsewhere
decisions.reason: The English gives the coins here without a measures setting, and the Amharic follows it: Literal and Balanced name the denarius, and Readable says "silver coins" as the English Readable does. "የብር ሳንቲም" is used so that "ብር" is not read as the Ethiopian birr.

source.text: μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο.

records.literal_gloss: Not having they to repay, both he forgave.

en.L: When they did not have [the means] to repay, he freely forgave [them] both.
en.B: Neither of them could pay him back, so he freely canceled the debts of both.
en.R: Neither of them had the money to pay him back. So he kindly canceled what both of them owed.

es.L: Como no tenían [con qué] pagar, les perdonó [la deuda] a ambos.
